subject: Clarification: SOC 2 audit period boundary for multi-region services
messages:
From: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@locke-audit.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Audit window — timezone & partial-month question

Hi Jordan,

Quick question as we prepare the Type II work for Kestrel: your SOC 2 report lists the period as 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30. The control testing plan needs a clear definition of what "inclusive of 2024-06-30" means operationally across regions. Specifically:

- For services with multi-region endpoints (us-east-1 and eu-west-1), do you treat the audit cutoff as 2024-06-30 23:59:59 UTC, or 2024-06-30 local time per region?
- For logs and streaming telemetry, should we interpret the snapshot point as ingestion timestamp or event occurrence timestamp?
- If some evidence only exists for a trailing fraction of the month (e.g., logs retained starting 2024-06-30 02:00 UTC due to migration), would you be able to provide a bridge letter or a point-in-time assertion?

If you can confirm the cutoff definition and call out any known partial-coverage windows, we can finalize our sample selection and report language.

Thanks,
Evelyn Shaw
Senior Audit Manager — Locke & Partners
[evelyn.shaw@locke-audit.com]

Attachment: (none)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@locke-audit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit window — timezone & partial-month question

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the note and for flagging this early. Summary answers up front:

- Redwood uses UTC for control-testing cutoffs (we assert "end of day" as 23:59:59 UTC).
- For telemetry/log evidence we primarily reference ingestion timestamp in our central logging pipeline (GELF -> central ELK ingest time), but we can provide both ingestion and event timestamps for samples if the auditor prefers.
- We do have one small migration event on 2024-06-30 where some ingress was redirected between regions between 01:45–03:10 UTC; we can provide a bridge letter to explain that window and supplemental evidence for transactions routed during that interval.

I'll let Marissa provide the technical detail on the migration and the suggested wording for a bridge letter. Rishi — FYI on the ingestion vs event-ts mapping.

Jordan
Director, Customer Security (on behalf of Redwood Compliance Team)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2_TypeII_Report_2023-07-01_to_2024-06-30.pdf (report stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@locke-audit.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit window — timezone & partial-month question

Hi Evelyn,

Providing more detail on the technical side so you can document sampling: 

Context: on 2024-06-30 we executed a regional routing change to consolidate ephemeral ingress in eu-west-1 for a short migration. No control changes were made; this affected only traffic routing.

What we recommend auditors treat as evidence: 

- Cutoff definition: 2024-06-30 23:59:59 UTC (that is the timestamp used by our controls and the one included in the SOC 2 assertion).
- Logs: primary evidence is ingestion timestamp (index ingestion time in central ELK). Where needed we can extract event timestamps from application logs and include both times in the sample export.
- Controls dependent on a point-in-time (e.g., access lists, firewall rules): our internal snapshots are taken at 00:00 UTC daily; we can provide a snapshot file for 2024-06-30_00:00UTC for immutable configs.

Migration window (2024-06-30 01:45–03:10 UTC): 
- We have request/response traces for the affected services and a routing-change audit that shows the handover.
- Draft bridge letter attached (bridge_letter_draft_v1.docx) — language is short, states that the routing change was operational only and did not alter control design or effectiveness.

If that works for you, we can: 
1) Produce a log export with both ingestion and event timestamps for a small sample across that window.
2) Finalize and sign the bridge letter.
3) Share the config snapshot and the routing-change audit record.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Risk & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bridge_letter_draft_v1.docx (draft), routing-change-audit-20240630.log (attachment stub)

From: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@locke-audit.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kestrel Health <security@kestrelhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit window — timezone & partial-month question

Thanks — that's very helpful. Confirming next steps from the auditor side: 

- We will accept 23:59:59 UTC as the control cutoff and document that in the report language.
- Please provide the sample log export with ingestion + event timestamps for the migration window and the daily config snapshot for 2024-06-30_00:00UTC.
- The draft bridge letter looks fine; we'll propose one minor wording tweak (add the exact UTC window to the second paragraph). If you can push an updated Doc to the Drive link below and notify me when it's ready, we'll route it for signatures.

Drive link for uploads: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExampleAuditEvidence
Auditor portal (for sample uploads): https://app.locke-audit.com/portal/Kestrel-2027

I'll also attach a short evidence checklist (evidence_checklist_kestrel.xlsx) showing the fields we require for each log row (ingestion_ts, event_ts, request_id, user_id, route, region). Once we receive the exports we'll start sample selection.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Evelyn
Senior Audit Manager — Locke & Partners

Attachment: evidence_checklist_kestrel.xlsx (template)
